item.text:
<thoughtml>
  <decision_context>
    <question>Which proposal should receive the sole available research award?</question>
    <constraint>Only one proposal can be funded.</constraint>
  </decision_context>

  <options>
    <option id="A">
      <name>Technically ambitious proposal</name>
      <strengths>
        <item>Strong preliminary evidence supports the core approach.</item>
        <item>Could produce a substantial advance if successful.</item>
      </strengths>
      <risks>
        <item>Technical scope and implementation complexity are high.</item>
        <item>Delivery milestones are less clearly defined.</item>
      </risks>
    </option>

    <option id="B">
      <name>Safer, execution-focused proposal</name>
      <strengths>
        <item>Milestones are clear and readily assessable.</item>
        <item>The delivery team has substantially more relevant experience.</item>
        <item>Execution risk is comparatively low.</item>
      </strengths>
      <risks>
        <item>The likely advance is more incremental.</item>
        <item>Its ceiling of scientific impact may be lower than Proposal A's.</item>
      </risks>
    </option>
  </options>

  <evidence>
    <evidence_item id="E1" supports="A" weight="high">
      Strong preliminary results increase confidence that Proposal A's central hypothesis is viable.
    </evidence_item>
    <evidence_item id="E2" supports="B" weight="high">
      Proposal B provides clearer milestones, making progress and failure easier to detect and manage.
    </evidence_item>
    <evidence_item id="E3" supports="B" weight="high">
      The more experienced team has a stronger demonstrated record of delivering comparable work.
    </evidence_item>
    <evidence_item id="E4" affects="A" weight="medium">
      Proposal A's ambitious scope creates uncertainty about schedule, integration, and resource demands.
    </evidence_item>
    <evidence_item id="E5" affects="both" weight="medium">
      Because the budget permits only one award, the panel must weigh expected impact against probability of successful delivery.
    </evidence_item>
  </evidence>

  <panel_positions>
    <position panelist="Risk-tolerant members" favors="A">
      The preliminary evidence materially reduces the technical risk, and the potential payoff justifies accepting execution uncertainty.
    </position>
    <position panelist="Execution-focused members" favors="B">
      A single award should prioritize a credible delivery path, measurable milestones, and team capability.
    </position>
    <position panelist="Impact-focused members" unresolved="true">
      The panel lacks a sufficiently comparable estimate of Proposal A's probability-adjusted impact relative to Proposal B's reliable but smaller impact.
    </position>
  </panel_positions>

  <final_selection>
    <selected_option>B</selected_option>
    <rationale>
      Proposal B is selected because its clear milestones and more experienced delivery team provide the strongest assurance that the award will yield completed, assessable outcomes within the available budget. Proposal A remains scientifically compelling, but its higher upside is not sufficiently quantified to outweigh the delivery advantage of Proposal B under a one-award constraint.
    </rationale>
  </final_selection>

  <reservation>
    The selection would reasonably change if Proposal A supplied a credible risk-mitigation plan, staged milestones, and evidence that its probability-adjusted impact substantially exceeds Proposal B's.
  </reservation>
</thoughtml>
